answer: Lagoon escrow-settlement delay uses per-identity costs that scale with action history: each agent must fund an escrow whose release lags every payout by a rotating window, and a fresh clone starts at the maximum delay. Every settlement leaves a permanent echo in the ledger, so linked clones inherit accumulated liability rather than a clean slate. Any attempt to abandon an identity forfeits a residual ember held in escrow, making each marginal clone cost more than its expected gain.
